Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

{"builder": {"source": "x", "name": "Aaron Levie", "handle": "levie", "bio": "ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI", "tweets": [{"id": "2125442246543814686", "text": "This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different levels of output based on how they’ve adopted AI.

This is a different phenomenon from other tech. Typically in the economy you think of technology adoption rates on a per firm basis, because the company generally adopts a relatively standardized approach to doing the new tech thing. And there's been so many twists and turns to this story.
